findings.title: Where you stand this month
findings.explanation: Your liquid cash is $3,650.00 against the $1,500.00 floor you chose, covering about 1.21 months of essentials. In a typical month $1,503.50 is left after commitments and usual spending; in a low month it is $533.50.

findings.title: Your income is irregular, so the low month is the one to plan around
findings.explanation: Across 6 observed months your income varied enough to count as irregular. The outlook already uses the lowest month for your irregular stream; budgets built on the average will feel tight in slow months.
findings.suggested_next_action: Treat the low month as your planning income.

findings.title: Your reserve is below the target you set
findings.explanation: You are $2,399.00 short of your own buffer target. This is your target, not a rule; it matters because a buffer is what keeps a slow month from becoming card debt.
findings.suggested_next_action: Decide a monthly pace for the reserve in Next steps.

findings.title: Paying extra on Rewards credit card would avoid $3,026.04 in interest
findings.explanation: Compared with minimums only, the highest-rate-first path on your stated extra payment avoids $3,026.04 of interest and finishes 32 months sooner. The trade-off is less cash each month, which is why the buffer question comes first.
findings.suggested_next_action: Compare the paths in Scenarios before choosing a pace.

findings.title: Several essential payments land in the same week
findings.explanation: 2 essential payments totalling $1,760.00 fall between 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-07. Timing causes most short-term squeezes; knowing the week lets you set the money aside from the previous income.

findings.title: Why the buffer question comes before the debt question
findings.explanation: A reserve covers a slow month without new borrowing; interest savings from extra payments only help if the payment never has to be reversed with a card. The Learn section walks through this trade-off with your own numbers.
